Latin word

mantēle

mantēle, mantēlis n.

noun, third declension

hand towel; hand towel, napkin; tablecloth, in a later sense

In this lexicon

  • hand towel

    the recommended word · classical · Varr. LL 6.85: mantēlium, ubi manūs terguntur; Verg. A. 1.702

  • napkin

    also used · classical · Varr. LL VI 85; Verg. A. I 702

  • tablecloth

    also used · post-classical · Isidore, Orig. 19.26.6; Trebellius Pollio (Lewis & Short); Traupman 125

Notes

  1. 1The hand towel is mantēle: Varr. LL 6.85 mantēlium, ubi manūs terguntur; Verg. A. 1.702. Not manutergium, which only Isidore has. Ruling: linteum and mantēle.

Examples

  • Postrēmō Theodōrus epitonium, quod ipse verterat, ipse clausit ōsque mantēlī tersit.

    Finally Theo turned off the tap he had turned on himself and wiped his mouth on the hand towel.Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam
